layers.name: Edge
layers.what: Traefik is the single entry point for all public and internal traffic, reachable directly and from behind WireGuard. The firewall drops unsolicited traffic to the public IP, a few hosts are published through Cloudflare so floods never reach the router, and Tailscale runs on every instance as a failover VPN in case WireGuard goes down.

layers.name: Identity
layers.what: Authentik is the single sign-on for the whole lab — OAuth, SAML and LDAP, down to the NAS logins.

layers.name: Compute
layers.what: Proxmox runs the LXC containers and VMs, declared in OpenTofu instead of clicked together in the web UI.

layers.name: Network
layers.what: RouterOS is code as well — firewall rules and the WireGuard peers I use to get back in from outside.

layers.name: Inventory
layers.what: NetBox is the source of truth for devices, prefixes and VLANs, and it is managed as code like everything else.

layers.name: Secrets
layers.what: Vault hands out the credentials stacks need at runtime, so nothing sensitive sits in git or in Terraform state.

layers.name: Observability
layers.what: Grafana and VictoriaMetrics are provisioned from config, Blackbox probes 25+ endpoints, and alerts route to Telegram and email.

layers.name: Home
layers.what: Home Assistant with Zigbee2MQTT and Mosquitto, plus n8n for the automations that stitch services together.

layers.name: Media
layers.what: Jellyfin and the *arr stack, with the downloaders routed through a VPN gateway container.

operations.name: One way to change things
operations.what: Every OpenTofu module carries the same Makefile — init, plan, apply, validate, fmt — and remote state lives in a GCS bucket.

operations.name: Nothing on :latest
operations.what: Images and providers are pinned to explicit versions and bumped by Renovate, so an upgrade arrives as a reviewable diff instead of a surprise at 2am.

operations.name: Guardrails before merge
operations.what: Pre-commit hooks run alongside consistency and security-invariant checks, so the obvious mistakes never reach the host.

operations.name: Restore from the repo
operations.what: Stacks ship env templates and seed config, so a service comes back from git rather than from memory.

operations.name: Hermes does the chores
operations.what: OpenCode and Hermes handle the day-to-day. Hermes watches for new versions across the lab, and when an upgrade has no breaking changes it commits and applies it to the repo itself — monitoring keeps an eye on the rollout, and a failed check triggers an automatic rollback.

operations.name: Secrets stay out of git
operations.what: Stacks commit only .env.example skeletons; the real values are injected at runtime by Vault — including the OAuth client secrets Authentik depends on, so there is nothing sensitive sitting in state either.

operations.name: The house answers messages
operations.what: Family can message the Facebook page and get Home Assistant to act: n8n verifies Meta's webhook, maps the sender to a person with their own conversation thread, and calls the HA conversation API. A Cloudflare rule exception lets Meta's servers through the geo-block so it works at all.
